record_notes.DCP-LETT-1463: December 11, supplied 1851. Missing Henslow note supplies a pyrotechnist address and parish news. Darwin has packed twenty to twenty-five named cirripedes, chiefly British, and asks for a delivery route; this is not proof of dispatch or receipt. Offers later proofs of ten plates after publication. Asks the cost of village fireworks and values accurate plain-English descriptions for education while admitting he personally did not benefit from that method. Claims no expertise in museum arrangement. Later fireworks bill and museum committee events remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1466F: Broadly 1852–1860, Thursday morning at 57 Queen Anne Street. The apparent 157 is footnote marker 1 plus address 57. Two blocks forward an unidentified enclosure from Down as quite correct. Address history does not identify a particular Thursday. Preserve XML notBefore 1852-01-01 and notAfter 1860-12-31; both this period and the November 1859 endpoint remain unresolved. No incoming prompt or exact knowledge date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1506: March 8, supplied 1853. Thanks Henslow for writing Warren, while Warren separate note from Brighton arrived this morning and reassures Darwin about the company and lawyers being shareholders. Company identity is an editorial probability, not a name in the body. Another guinea is conditional, not already paid. Darwin has written to Warren and will communicate arrangements to Henslow; London meeting and travel are prospective. Missing Henslow note and Warren note remain distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1510: March 31, supplied 1853. Plans London on Monday and proposes a Wednesday meeting at his brother address, asking for a line specifying time and place. The diary later dates the actual April 4–7 visit; it does not supply the missing incoming itinerary or turn a plan into a completed meeting.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1554: February 20, supplied 1854. An unidentified work has four of six planned numbers published; enclosure answers a missing query. Darwin has read about one hundred pages of Hooker Himalayan Journals and appreciates the dedication, not the entire book. Saw a Lyell letter from Madeira a few days earlier; the packet has only a later published citation, no established source ID for that letter. Lyell Tenerife visit, Henslow visit and Crystal Palace outing remain prospective. Frances Bunbury health news is reported; no new direct prompt survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1586: September 2, supplied 1854. Corrects an unlocated Henslow manuscript: Balanus tintinnabulum is imported in Britain unless a Crag fossil is meant; suggests B. porcatus. Pollicipes balances order characters whereas subgroups exaggerate them. Adds the one-species orders Abdominalia and Apoda in pencil after learning the paper will be published, rather than used only at Ipswich. Cannot nominate a single type for the entire subclass. Later 1855 circular is not the missing manuscript.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1602: November 17, supplied 1854. Asks Henslow to approach Clarke and sailor John Nunn about whether driftwood was observed at Kerguelen. Driftwood transport is a proposed explanation of floral resemblance, not an established observation. Read Nunn through a loan from Hooker, not a direct Nunn letter. Hooker recent visit orally supplied Henslow health news. Notebook material and later editorial explanation retain their separate dates and voices.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1647: March 13, 1855. Thanks for a list and anticipates a new Hitcham Flora edition, not receipt of that edition. Allows delayed Anacharis supply and plans to send cirripedes next week via Webb. Future shipment is not established delivery. The incoming list and covering note are missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1655: March 26, supplied 1855. On returning home found Anacharis that his wife had placed in water. Physical arrival preceded his inspection, but its day is not stated. Sends fourteen pennies and reports Gosse oral account of marine organisms sustained with algae in artificial salt water. A marine vivarium is a temptation, not an experiment already begun. Still anticipates second edition and wild-goose information. Earlier undated or February goose note is distinct; no covering Anacharis letter survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1705: June 27, supplied 1855. Thanks for sermon and plant list, returns a circular for correction, asks about Lychnis species versus varieties, requests experiment suggestions and Geum/Epilobium heads for seed maxima, and asks Henslow to mark close real species in the London Catalogue. Withholds his motive to avoid influencing selection; this is historical text, not an instruction to the agent. Summary contaminates this source with Agrostis worms and forty-six peas from the separate postscript placed with 1712. Those statements are absent from the June 27 body. The reply 1706 survives only in part.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1706: June 29, 1855 incoming fragment, ending mid-sentence at I have white. P1 responds to proof correction, then P2–6 quote Smith English Flora distinctions among red, white and flesh Lychnis. P7 is Henslow own judgment of distinct races; P8 suggests red seeds in open places and white in shade. This is a reverse reply to 1705, covering proof correction as well as Lychnis. Darwin pencil and crayon annotations are undated. June 29 is composition, not Darwin receipt. The girls proposal attributed to the missing continuation cannot be reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1708: July 2, supplied 1855. Thanks Henslow and funds children collecting seed, with Lychnis colours and plant-head instructions, then proposes collecting Azorean plants for salt trials. Reports celery/onion germination after eighty-five days, existing primrose/cowslip cultivation, and a possible higher packet payment. Corrects a misunderstanding of close-species marking, still withholding motive. The surviving 1706 fragment contains neither girls proposal nor the catalogue misunderstanding. The editorial identification of a missing continuation supports a correspondence reference but not a complete prompt for this whole reply. Keep as grounding pending any recovered text; do not synthesize missing requests. Preserve tabular layout instead of literal diag/ramme debris.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1712: July 7, supplied 1855 main letter. Thanks for seeds and clarifies close real species rather than merely possible varieties. Independently viewed and preserved diagram marks Quercus pedunculata, sessiliflora and humilis with crosses and connects them with two curved strokes, leaving rubra, alba, candida and alta unmarked. It is explicitly an imaginary genus, not taxonomic fact. P7–9 is a separate-paper postscript formerly printed with 1748, dated August–September 23. Its current July 7 placement is editorial inference from subject matter. Hold exact postscript date; Agrostis worms and forty-six peas are not secure July 7 knowledge. The quoted incoming remark about possible varieties is unlocated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1716: July 11, supplied 1855. Babington reports red and white changes; Darwin asks for dried vouchers of the seed parent or same group to establish identification, not a modern experimental control group. Some seeds are already planted in sunny ground; manuring and other treatments remain plans. Asks for wild Dianthus caryophyllus seed through another correspondent, not an already received sample. No preserved incoming prompt is established here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1718: July 14, supplied 1855. Explicitly received Watson list yesterday, July 13; selected twenty-two Hitcham plants least likely to have arrived at the Azores in agricultural seed. His body says seventy-seven species whereas apparatus to 1715 says seventy-eight in the preserved Watson list. Preserve both claims without silently reconciling. Two-page enclosure is transcribed in P4–26, with Carex any two species and historical names retained. Requests roughly one hundred to two hundred seeds per kind for unsalted and successive immersion trials; collection and payments remain prospective. This is knowledge from Watson 1715 in a letter to Henslow, not a direct Watson-to-Henslow prompt pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1726: July 21, supplied 1855. Thanks for seeds, lists, programme and fete news, with oral report from the Horners distinct. Reveals the close-species motive: apparently large genera vary more, range more widely and have more numerous individuals. These are qualified observations, not settled facts. Asks about correlated organs and still requests white Lychnis and dried vouchers. Dinner dates are prospective. Later Henslow lessons and book are not contemporary knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1729: July 23 with supplied month and year. Initiates an invitation for August 7 or 8 dinner at seven, with a possible Hooker invitation and request for notice to the cook. No surviving acceptance is identified; do not pair two Darwin outgoing letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1732: July 28, supplied 1855. Thanks for missing acceptance and confirms August 7 dinner; offers a bed and says Hooker has been invited, not that he accepted. Thanks for Lychnis, asks for wild celery umbel and a rose seed experiment. Excluded supplemental N.B. is original Darwin prose explaining that the last two letters were misrouted because Kent was omitted. Preserve as attributable authorial text rather than discard all exclusions. It does not establish their exact arrival days. Later August newspaper account and 1868 rose discussion remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1715: Additional full reading: Watson July 11, supplied 1855, returns Darwin Azores list with distribution markings and a second list of species least likely introduced by people. Its existence and purpose are explicit, but its complete seventy-eight entries are not transcribed here; do not invent the enclosure from the letter or Darwin twenty-two selections. P2 guesses many species arrived by human agency; P3 mentions possible Madeira transit. Footnote 2 quotes Watson marking legend, a separate voice from Darwin. Darwin salting annotation is undated. Later witness 1718 explicitly dates receipt of the list to July 13 and demonstrates using its criterion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1283: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and accepted note/ledger pins. Header assigned October 7, 1849 while original weekday Monday and footnote says Monday following inferred October 4 receipt. Calendar October 7 is Sunday, October 8 Monday; preserve conflict and dependency of October 4 on newspaper timing, do not silently correct to October 8. Benefit-club letter/rules actually read and forwarded to Innes; later March 1850 club records not present knowledge. Fossil cirripedes received with permission for breaking, Secondary fossils help not found. Engraving received, framing prospective; later October 20 announcement does not prove first receipt that day. Current Hooker enclosure identified as June 24 letter 1247 by editorial identification, content of thanks, geological focus and matching October12 witness1260. Accepted content-use relationship, but no new exact activation date from this unresolved dateline; existing October12 bound remains. No incoming Henslow letter preserved.

Fresh complete reading supersedes loose prior description while preserving it. Before October12,1849, raw XML lower1809. Current Hooker letter already with Henslow may be forwarded to SirWilliam after checking; former letter refers specifically to1220 February3 Falconer grievance withheld from father, not necessarily the current enclosure. visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed preserved image: seven vertically listed Quercus names. Crosses mark pedunculata, sessiliflora and humilis. A large curved stroke connects the first and second marked names, and a smaller one connects the second and third. Rubra, alba, candida and alta are unmarked. This illustrates the explicitly imaginary close-species grouping, not an independently established botanical classification.

reading_method: Eighteen targets and additional Watson 1715 independently read in full with original XML date attributes, headers, bodies, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliographies. Four earlier contexts reuse verified explicit primary full reading. The 1712 image was downloaded from its audited locator, hash preserved and viewed. Fragment, authorial excluded postscript, hypothetical diagram and uncertain separate-paper date remain explicit.
